clue.text: One of the first colonies to achieve prompt liquidation of debts?

explanation.surface: A pioneering colony is praised for paying off what it owes quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: An early settlement is a primitive colony; a settlement made early is a debt paid off promptly.

clue.text: Debate that never reaches any conclusion

definitions.text: Debate that never reaches any conclusion

parts.words: Debate that never reaches any conclusion
parts.note: a dispute that goes round and round, read literally as a quarrel with no end to it

explanation.definitionFit: A row that never finishes is a dispute without an ending, the literal and figurative senses coinciding.

clue.text: He has no wish to confer with others about tortuous clues

definitions.text: He has no wish to confer with others

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: tortuous means twisting, so the letters of the next word are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shuns conversation because the clues are too convoluted to discuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like part of the surface, but it supplies its own letters; 'tortuous' is the anagram signal for clues.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit or loner is someone who avoids company and conversation.

clue.text: They grow starchy in tropical lands

definitions.text: They grow starchy in tropical lands

parts.words: They grow starchy in tropical lands
parts.note: describes edible starchy tubers cultivated in hot countries

explanation.definitionFit: These tubers are a staple root crop of hot climates, rich in starch.

clue.text: Produce a big picture?

parts.note: reads like making an epic film, but means blowing up a photograph to a larger size

explanation.definitionFit: In photography, to blow up a print is to make it bigger.

clue.text: Oft-varied charges for sweetmeats

indicators.note: varied means changed in form, so the letters of oft are rearranged

parts.note: fees are charges made for a service

explanation.surface: A confectioner keeps changing the prices of sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oft-varied' reads as a hyphenated adjective, but 'varied' is the anagram signal acting on oft.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewy caramel sweets are a kind of confectionery, an old word for which is sweetmeats.

clue.text: Perfectly original plot?

parts.note: plot means a piece of ground rather than a story: the first, perfect garden of Genesis

explanation.definitionFit: The biblical garden was the original paradise, a flawless first patch of land.

clue.text: Guaranteed without doubt in the finish

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the end is the finish
sure means certain, without doubt

explanation.surface: Victory was certain right to the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without doubt' reads as an adverb for the definition but supplies its own letters, which 'in' places inside the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To have made certain of something is to have secured or assured it.

clue.text: Big bird on its way to pick up and carry heavy objects?

definitions.text: to pick up and carry heavy objects?

explanation.surface: A large wading bird migrates, perhaps carrying things as it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged bird in transit is literally a migrating crane; a gantry hoist that moves on rails lifts and carries loads.

clue.text: The hard cash that is needed to keep metrication going

definitions.text: The hard cash that is needed to keep metrication going

parts.words: The hard cash that is needed to keep metrication going
parts.note: hard cash means actual coins, the currency system based on tens that went with Britain's move to metric

explanation.definitionFit: Britain's 1971 switch to a pounds-and-pence system based on tens was the money side of going metric.

clue.text: The South African flag

parts.note: flag here is an iris-like plant, so a fragrant bloom native to South Africa, not a national banner

explanation.definitionFit: This scented flower of the iris family is native to southern Africa; flag is a name for iris-family plants.

clue.text: They can't fly me back to the land of the 13

indicators.note: back means the word me is written backwards

parts.note: the USA grew from thirteen original colonies

explanation.surface: Flightless creatures plead to be sent home to America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ME into EM. The thirteen are the original American colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: These large Australian birds are flightless runners.

clue.text: A West German city judge?

explanation.surface: A question about which city in West Germany might act as a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Trier is an ancient city on the Moselle in (then) West Germany; one who tries a case is literally a judge.

clue.text: At liberty to go about breaking iron

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open the iron symbol to hold another piece

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A prisoner is let loose to roam, smashing his iron chains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' pictures smashing chains; here it means one piece cuts the iron symbol open.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unconfined or not imprisoned is to be at liberty.

clue.text: The first cardinal canonised in Staffordshire?

parts.note: a canonised person is a saint, abbreviated St
the first cardinal number is one

explanation.surface: Asks which churchman was the first to be made a saint in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: The cardinal is a number, not a churchman. The definition is by example: Stone is a market town in Staffordshire, an English Midlands county.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town in the English Midlands county of Staffordshire bears this name.

clue.text: Poetical conception of long division

parts.note: long division sounds like arithmetic, but means a section of a long poem

explanation.definitionFit: A long poem such as Dante's is divided into numbered sections with this name.

clue.text: He sat around before he put the sword away

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the letters of he sat are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man sat about a while before laying down his weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the anagram signal on 'He sat', not a word about sitting nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: To return a blade to its scabbard is to encase it.

clue.text: Malicious gossip can get boys turned out

indicators.note: out here means outside, so the reversed boys go round the can
turned means the boys are written backwards

parts.note: lads are boys

explanation.surface: Spiteful rumours can lead to boys being expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes LADS into SDAL, and 'out' puts it outside CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A disgraceful rumour or outrage spread maliciously is a source of public shame.

clue.text: Fellow I caught going after river duck of Latin origin

indicators.note: going after says the fellow, I and caught follow the river and duck

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
a man is a fellow
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A man catches a duck by a river; the bird turns out to be of Latin descent.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Languages descended from Latin, such as French and Italian, are called Romance or Romanic.

clue.text: Kind of pickaxe an abstainer has to jeer about

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so jeer wraps round the abstainer

parts.note: to mock is to jeer
TT is teetotal, a person abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: A digging tool belongs to a teetotaller who must put up with teasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A TT inside MOCK. TT, teetotal, is a crossword convention for an abstainer.
explanation.definitionFit: This digging tool has a blade like an adze on one side and a pick on the other.

clue.text: See 9
The sponge-cake's cousin?

parts.note: sponge suggests a bath sponge, so its relative is named after a bath, while also being a sweet yeasted bun from an English spa city

explanation.definitionFit: This sweet currant bun from the English spa city of Bath is a relation of sponge cake in the baking family.

clue.text: Grotesque sort of brazier

indicators.note: sort here means arrange, so the letters of brazier are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Describes an ugly, strange kind of metal fire-basket.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weird or outlandish is grotesque.

clue.text: Salad-dressing swallowed by C a dandy French critic

indicators.note: swallowed by means the dressing goes inside the dandy

parts.note: a beau is a fashionable dandy
oil is a salad dressing

explanation.surface: A fop gulps down salad dressing, as a French critic might.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicolas Boileau was a 17th-century French poet and critic; the stray 'C' in the printed clue gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicolas Boileau-Despréaux was a famous French literary critic of the 1600s.

clue.text: As far as could be from the Mount of Olives

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the words Mount of

explanation.surface: Measuring a distance from the hill near Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points to the letters inside 'Mount of'.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic preposition means 'to' or 'up to', as in 'even unto the end'.

clue.text: The man who had Gladstone reeling?

explanation.surface: Which politician left his great rival Gladstone staggering?
explanation.walkthrough: Disraeli, Gladstone's Victorian rival as Prime Minister, was nicknamed Dizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli's nickname, the rival who bested Gladstone; the word also means giddy or staggering.

clue.text: A record seen when the moon is full

definitions.text: seen when the moon is full

explanation.surface: A record sighted under a full moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is a flat circle; at full moon its whole face appears as a round plate.

clue.text: Aggressive style of writing?

parts.note: a clenched hand is aggressive, and the same word is old slang for a person's handwriting

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a clenched hand and, informally, one's handwriting.

clue.text: A boy of four getting nothing right

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A four-year-old boy gets no answers correct.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Welsh boy's name, as in Ivor Novello.

clue.text: The blue books kept under the counter at the library?

definitions.text: The blue books kept under the counter at the library?

parts.words: The blue books kept under the counter at the library?
parts.note: blue means indecent rather than a colour, and under the counter means hidden from view

explanation.definitionFit: Racy or pornographic literature is called blue, and is often kept out of sight.

clue.text: I arrive all dishevelled in the South of France

indicators.note: dishevelled means untidy and messed up, so the letters of I arrive are jumbled

explanation.surface: A traveller turns up rumpled on the French coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean coast of southern France is known as the Côte d'Azur.

clue.text: Travel by main road?

parts.note: main is an old word for the open sea, so its road is a shipping lane, not a highway

explanation.definitionFit: To go by ship across the ocean, the main being the high sea.
